follow-up time: 4 years (2 years pre-training and 2 years post-training)
exposure: Clinics that received training (cases) and clinics that did not (referents)
Advances in Labour and Risk Management (ALARM) International Program (AIP)
Emergency obstetric care training using Advances in Labour and Risk Management (ALARM) International Program (AIP)
cohort: Obstetric providers from 64 maternity clinics in Ukraine
finding: Emergency obstetric care training was associated with a significant reduction in postpartum hemorrhage-related interventions (blood transfusions, plasma transfusions, and uterus explorations), but also with an increase in vacuum extraction, forceps-assisted delivery, and Cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Emergency obstetric care training was associated with an increase in vacuum extraction, forceps-assisted delivery, and Cesarean sections.
